subject: Stratosphere - activation exception for priority sprint
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Stratosphere - activation exception for priority sprint

Hi team,

Quick ask from the Stratosphere deal (SF-2026-1178) — they just confirmed a $1.2M ARR commitment if we can guarantee a short runway for an enterprise-only activation behavior that is not in our current product roadmap. Specifically they need:

- Per-tenant model affinity and warm-cache pinning for a 30-minute window during peak hours.
- A guarantee that their audit export (full request/response traces for 30 days) can be delivered without increasing tail latency beyond our SLA.

They've escalated timing: they want a canary in our Nov sprint with full availability by mid-December. Sales/CS are already committing this as a commercial term contingent on a technical exception.

Attached: Stratosphere_Audit_Sheet.xlsx (request details) and a draft SOW (SOW_draft_v3.pdf).

Asking for directional feasibility and a tradeoff summary we can show the customer (eng effort, risk, and whether we can do a gated canary). Can Jordan weigh in on complexity and Marissa on product acceptability? Priyom, Im looping you for contract implications.

Thanks,
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0129
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stratosphere - activation exception for priority sprint

Thanks for the context and attachments — read through the audit sheet. Two immediate product-level concerns:

1) Per-tenant model affinity + pinning is effectively a policy layer we haven't productized; we currently have instance affinity via residency but not a 30-minute guaranteed warm cache window.

2) Delivering 30-day full request/response traces with near-zero impact on tail latency is possible but will require an isolated export pipeline or on-demand export throttling.

Before we commit to a sprint exception, I need:
- A scoped engineering estimate (T-shirt: S/M/L and an LOE in dev-weeks).
- A proposed canary plan: feature flag, safety rollbacks, and telemetry to validate SLA impact.
- A suggested wording for the commercial SOW that limits blast radius if we need to rollback.

Jordan — can you give a quick feasibility note? Priyom — any contractual redlines we should pre-empt?

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Group PM, Inference Platform | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: Sam Green <sam.green@stratosphere.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@stratosphere.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Stratosphere - activation exception for priority sprint

Aditya / Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 30-minute pin is to avoid cold-start variance during our daily market open window (09:30-10:30 ET).
- If a short canary is necessary, we can start with a 5% traffic slice and expand.
- We are flexible on who performs the export delivery; if Redwood provides a downloadable export on-demand (we trigger and retrieve), that's acceptable for our audit team.

We need this to appear in the SOW as a time-boxed activation exception (we understand its not yet GA). Can you propose language that limits ongoing support obligations?

Cheers,
Sam
Sam Green
Head of Platform Engineering | Stratosphere AI
sam.green@stratosphere.ai
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stratosphere - activation exception for priority sprint

Short feasibility readout from eng:

- Per-tenant affinity + short-duration warm-cache pinning: doable as a sprint-sized scoped effort (estimate: 3 engineers x 3 weeks to deliver a gated canary + feature flag + basic observability). Level: Medium risk because we will touch cache eviction and scheduling subsystems.

- Audit export: we can provide an on-demand export pipeline that writes sanitized request/response logs to a customer-specific S3 bucket (or share a signed link) without changing runtime path; estimated effort: 2 engineers x 2 weeks to wire export, plus 1 week to add throttles and monitoring.

Constraints / mitigations:
- Need a performance safety net: limit pinned capacity per tenant and auto-throttle if tail latency rises above X ms.
- We should call this an "activation exception" with a strict sunset (e.g., 90 days) unless productizes. That reduces long-term support obligation.

If we proceed, I recommend a 2-week engineering canary behind feature flags starting with 5% traffic, with a pre-defined rollback criterion and a post-canary SLA validation run.

Jordan
Jordan Blake
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stratosphere - activation exception for priority sprint

Thanks for the estimates — that LOE looks reasonable. From a commercial perspective:

- We can include a time-boxed activation exception clause in the SOW that explicitly calls out: scope, canary dates, success metrics, rollback terms, and a sunset (90 days).
- Recommend adding an engineering change buffer and an SLA carve-out: if we exceed X ms tail latency during the exception window and its attributable to the pinned behavior, Redwood will have a 72-hour remediation window.
- We should tie final acceptance to a short joint test plan (Redwood + Stratosphere) and an explicit sign-off to avoid open-ended support ask.

Next steps: Aditya — can you send a short SOW paragraph and proposed canary calendar? Marissa/Jordan — confirm final LOE and whether this needs an expedited sprint slot (I can re-prioritize).

PT: I added a 10% contingency to the LOE in case of unforeseen infra work.

– Priyom
